issue_context.title: planner: NullEQ cannot be used for composite indexes
comments:
The root cause is that TiKV can depend on the attributes `unique` and `point` to choose different storage access interfaces to speed up:
```
if Req.Index.IsUnique() && Req.Range.IsPoint() {
    store.Get(Req.Range.StartKey(), &results)
} else {
    store.Scan(Req.Range.Begin(), Range.End(), &results)
}
```
If the index is `unique` and the range is a `point` then it can assume that there is only 1 row to return and then it uses the faster interface `Get` instead of the general interface `Scan`.

But In MySQL, a `unique` index can have multiple duplicated records with `NULL`:
```
mysql> create table t (a int, b int, unique key(a, b));
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)

mysql> insert into t values (null, 1), (null, 1);
Query OK, 2 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from t;
+------+------+
| a    |  b   |
+------+------+
| NULL |  1   |
| NULL |  1   |
+------+------+
2 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

So if the range has `NULL`, the `1 row` assumption are broken.

review_comments: Maybe it is better to insert each value twice expect (1,1,1). In this way we can check whether it returns multiple rows (expected)  or just a single row(wrong).
What would happen if we don't add this line.
Then the default value `true` is used and some plans in this test cases will change.
This doesn't affect the correctness, right?
Will we remove the hard-code operation in the following PRs?
Yep, I plan to remove this hard-code operation with the switch `tidb_regard_null_as_point` together a few months later if there is no new bug.
